source_receiving_annotation_history.judgment: Sena reports the lord’s house destroyed, no one injured and the lord sheltered in the basement (P36–44). K’s relief at no deaths does not erase property harm. Dust’s negative evaluation is attributed speech (P138), not an omniscient moral certificate. No Maxwell actor or directed mechanism is shown.

Aqua repeats Darkness’s warning about the lord and predicts abuse of power (P168); preserve the nested report and future modality. Sena initially revises suspicion after the bell remains silent about accidental targeting (P234–239), then resumes inquiry when K’s denial of executive contact rings because of Wiz (P270–276). These corrections and ambiguity counter a simple claim that every officer is knowingly fabricating everything.

P354 gives accuser’s full name Alexei Barnes Alderp (アレクセイ・バーネス・アルダープ). He evaluates K, looks over three women, reacts particularly to Darkness and keeps watching her (P355–372); descriptions of lechery retain K’s perceptual framing. Mansion loss/inn residence and illegal dangerous teleport are prosecution statements (P371–373). Witnesses report actual harms while attempted contextual qualifications are curtailed; this does not establish a conspiracy known to all witnesses.

Alderp himself demands death (P15–17), loses momentum when K’s denial does not ring (P19–25), repeats his demand (P27) and stares at Sena before her confused reversal (P30–36). Aqua reports malign interference (P38); exact operator/mechanism remains unidentified here. Alderp turns pale after her detection (P51), but his private explanation is not stated. The judge actually pronounces death (P55–59); execution is not performed. Darkness’s crest and broad personal-obligation offer secure a delay, not withdrawal or acquittal (P78–96). Alderp initially protests despite status, then accepts the benefit. Darkness reports his fixation since childhood, widowhood and repeated rejected marriage proposals (P99–100); these remain report. Her comic excitement does not grant general consent to his later acts. Compensation and proving innocence remain obligations (P109–123).

Darkness explicitly denies the group’s imagined sexual mistreatment and says her dress is her own (P74–79). At P88–93 she reports Alderp’s request for a meeting with his son; she explains her prior broad promise by confidence her father would refuse gross demands, but does not yet know why Alderp wants this marriage. His exact hidden motive must not be substituted for her current uncertainty. Her noble full name is given at P128. K’s attempted stripping and Aqua’s distress remain actual harmful conduct, despite his equipment-sale explanation.

K’s political/household explanations for Alderp are conjectures (P157–158). Darkness’s father is a distinct currently unnamed actor, excited about her apparent acceptance (P221–235), accepts K’s formal intervention and later is reported offering reward for a successful meeting (P271–284). Daughter reports his display of her childhood portrait and valued vase (P263,298); they are not observed complete purchase histories. Do not map this father to Balter.

P318 distinguishes Alderp’s son Balter from Darkness’s father; Darkness provides son’s full name アレクセイ・バーネス・バルター at P368. Father praises Balter while distinguishing him from Alderp, then revises requested assistance toward preventing public embarrassment (P318–338). Descriptions of Balter’s perfect character, study, early knighthood, correction of father and household treatment are reports (P368–378); Aqua says she personally received his food distribution (P370), also a report of past experience. Father’s sincerity/permission for K’s coercion is partly K inference (P398,442–445), not omniscient ethical authorization. Aqua explicitly objects to deciding Darkness’s life (P399–404).

Balter actually expresses concern (P456–457,473), self-introduces as eldest son helping land administration (P463), notices closeness and expresses envy (P509–528). His initial gendered refusal to duel (P549) gives way to a declared changed interest after coming intending to reject his father’s imposed match (P554), then actual fast technical attacks and repeated hits/bruising (P556–566). He concedes while technically superior because he will not keep hitting her (P570–579); not an account of no harm, universal pacifism or technical defeat. K’s belief that he misunderstands her response is narrator inference (P583). Balter also expresses interest in watching K fight (P591).

Balter voices a conventional wooden-sword/no-magic expectation (P607), is embarrassed by exposure and shocked by freezing (P613,622); these are local reactions, not inability in every unconventional battle. K’s later gambit occurs while he fears losing the strength/drain contest (P658–676). Any subsequent Balter claim that K was already winning needs comparison with this actual sequence.

Balter appraises K as offering the bet when already about to win (P3); that differs from K’s contemporaneous fear of losing in previous member, so retain a fallible observer rather than perfect strategic insight. Darkness’s father arrives with drinks and orders both men executed after seeing her state (P7–18); they explain and no execution occurs (P22). His wife’s death, solitary parenting and daughter’s earlier loneliness are his retrospective account (P28–35). Balter declares attraction and reciprocal-love interpretation (P40–48), which does not settle K/Darkness relationship. He withdraws after Darkness’s false pregnancy story and offers to tell Alderp he declined (P81–89); later reporting is not performed here. Father and Aqua believe the false pregnancy and are corrected after about30minutes (P95–97). Daughter’s anticipated unconscious sexual encounter is explicitly denied (P71–72). The unnamed father and Balter remain separate.

This member changes focalization Aqua→Megumin→Darkness→K. Darkness says Alderp has made no further approach since the match but doubts lasting abandonment (P77–78); she reports recent silence rather than a complete future disposition. K reports suspicion lifted through Sena’s eyewitness-based intervention after the Vanir battle (P89–95), while Sena’s public apology/award, compensation/debt deduction and40millionremainingpayment are actually presented (P84–87,118–125). Do not attribute forgiveness or payment acceptance personally to Alderp without further evidence. Vanir’s future trial prediction and commercial invitation are his own prospective speech (P177–179), not an already performed outcome. The same continuing Vanir is observed again; no new Maxwell scene is supplied.

Darkness’s absence triggers K’s imagined mistreatment and captive hypotheses (P8–14,69–84,448–450), not a witnessed sexual incident or imprisonment. These are explicitly qualified by her later denial in C3 P77–79. No hidden Alderp act is inserted from the imaginative premise. Other party conduct in these windows is not inherited as Alderp agency. The partial C2 windows do not claim a complete chapter reread.

Sena initially suspects a repeated pattern, accepts the party’s denial and honors refusal of help (P18–31), then thanks their volunteered cooperation (P90–99). K calls her earnest at P99; keep that as his interpretation. The lord’s compensation and proof-of-innocence obligations remain unresolved at P35. Aqua’s active ward, K’s wish to erase evidence and the actual monster problem are distinct from proved Alderp/Maxwell control. Do not make every later inquiry an act of conscious collusion or unlimited magical manipulation.

An unnamed former retainer explicitly calls Darkness’s father Ignis at P437. This secures the named father route at this later point, not an earlier MAIN03 reader name or royal identity. At the banquet Alderp interrupts rival suitors, demands honorific status from K and says his Axel house is still being rebuilt while he uses his capital residence (P467–488). He promotes Prince Jatice as the uniquely fitting match and describes prospective succession/children; K’s thought that he has abandoned his desire is a conjecture (P489–490), later contradicted by the focal interlude. The anonymous nobles’ applause, self-justification and other court conduct are not all Alderp’s voice. C2 is only a bounded P371–640 reread here.

Alderp receives the group with a guard, leering and complimenting Aqua; he treats her goddess assertion as a joke (P21–34). The guard’s exact warning about Megumin is only partly overheard (P38–42); his retreat, awkward compliments and appeal for help are actual, without an invented complete whispered message. His sarcastic permission for an indefinite stay is taken literally (P50–60). He actually tends a one-way bath mirror, sees a working view of the cleaning maid, proposes shared watching and argues high wages include harassment (P99–132). That is his coercive entitlement claim, not maid consent. K nearly accepts but discovery interrupts the handshake (P126–130). The mirror is smashed (P132); the passive sentence does not name the breaker. No naked maid or completed sexual act is inserted. Window repair stinginess is K’s guess (P89), not proved purchase intent.

K reports incoming complaints about Megumin’s explosions (P179), while the guests actually consume Alderp’s alcohol, demand household resources and impose long storytelling (P188–204). Alderp is visibly worn and begins withdrawing his indefinite invitation through Darkness (P199–203); real recipient costs coexist with his misconduct. K warns Chris about the lecherous lord’s possible response (P297), but the footsteps first bring Darkness (P306); no assault on Chris is depicted or assigned to Alderp.

Alderp actually arrives with a guard to investigate the night disturbance and asks what is happening (P344–357); K asks him for rescue, but a reply or rescue is not shown. Chris later reports two ownerless sacred objects acquired by an initially unnamed noble, one summoning random monsters without stated usage cost and one body-swapping (P575–589). K’s claim that the former owner died is his gloss (P577). Her treasure sensing at Alderp’s home and K’s Aqua-robe explanation do not yet prove every object’s location or donor identity. The report of Beldia’s original remit through Mitsurugi remains attributed, not a new independent test (P493–499).

K’s comparison of nobles’ sexual behavior is his generalization (P554), not a class-wide law or a new Alderp action. Claire calls the body-swap necklace a gift intended for Jatice (P565–571); the donor is not named there. Chris explains that death during a swap prevents return and describes serial youth/wealth theft as a possible use (P608–620). It remains an attributed mechanism and possibility, not a performed murder in this window. Her warnings about all power-holders (P625) are not a census. K’s prior misuse of the body swap remains adverse to her trust (P627–631); this does not repair a frozen principal score.

Chris says strong treasure signals came from the castle and Alderp’s home (P97), and K again attributes the house signal to Aqua’s robe (P98). The castle vault search does not find the summoning object (P119). Neither limited search nor treasure sensing is exhaustive absence or proof that Alderp has no object. Other theft/harassment in this window belongs to the relevant party actors, not Alderp.

The first-person focalizer is Alderp, established by the devil addressing him (P5–8). He repeatedly kicks the devil he calls Maks/マクス (P5–17); that nickname needs its explicit later Maxwell join, not a second persona. The devil states it cannot locate an unknown sacred object or undo a real seal (P12–13); no failed dispelling attempt or universal impotence is observed. Alderp’s judgments of stupidity/memory are his hostile account (P18–20,38), while the devil voices pleasure in his cruelty and desire for work/reward (P35). Alderp’s represented thought explicitly supplies the prince body-theft/marriage plan and regret over skipping a lower step (P21–32); the planned killing of his old body is prospective, not accomplished. He says he selected a handsome capable child and regards Balter as a prepared body resource (P29–32); Balter’s familial position is clear but biological origin/legal adoption details are not supplied. His claim everything previously went well (P22) is self-assessment, contradicted by his own current failures. He keeps this devil because memory lapses permit avoiding payment (P38–39), and actually holds the random-monster summoning stone (P41–46). It does not prove unlimited summoning or ordinary salary consent.

The guild actually pays the Sylvia bounty after delay (P8–16); this does not establish every executive killing or an independent character assessment. Darkness reports her father recently ill and says she avoids disturbing him with the endurance-contest practice (P119). No Alderp/Maxwell cause is supplied at that point. K’s reference to his earlier binding at Alderp’s house (P126) is a callback, not a new act of the lord. The egg merchant’s identity remains unprovided despite Aqua’s quoted sales story (P153 onward); no generic vendor join.

Vanir describes keeping Wiz working without rest/food and now resting her (P198–208); this is his account of the work arrangement, not a newly watched two-week history. His apparent prophecy of harm to the house/father, Darkness’s failed self-sacrifice and proposed escape remain future/conditional statements (P275–308), qualified by difficulty seeing through Aqua’s presence (P216) and his own capability claims (P290). Do not treat the father’s whole future as already performed, validate every class-wide claim, or rewrite any frozen Vanir forecast/score. Darkness visits home after the warning (P282–283).

An unnamed butler enters without introduction, insults the setting and names Alderp as his master, requesting Darkness come to his carriage (P325–336). His own delivery behavior is direct; no name or Ragcraft identity is supplied. The next day Darkness says she slept at her family home after the late appointment (P358–375), so K’s sexualized overnight speculation is not an observed affair. She avoids explaining the noble tie and urgently proposes a Hydra bounty with ecological warning and a later knight fallback (P365–425). The source shows her urgency and K’s uncertainty, not the exact secret contract at this point. Actual Hydra size exceeds the printed expectation and the party’s initial plan (P466–488); no hidden perfection is imputed to her.

COHORT28_MAKS_NICKNAME_NUMBER_RETRIEVAL_01.json SHA256 8d98159da7c01f6f3af6787863dc05ac93beebbe6f35bee1ead00d2a2fdbffb2 checks all41 current native/register pins and finds four literal-stem resources. This routes the MAIN06 I nickname plus MAIN07 I, MAIN16 C1 and YORI04 U007. It supplies zero semantic-context or independent credit and no exhaustive anonymous absence.

The guild actually pays the party a Hydra bounty share and extra contribution (P6–30); Darkness is absent. Her note says she is reporting the kill to the lord, and the house’s rebuild is K’s present understanding (P48–49). K’s belief the noble would not act against her status is not validated protection (P83). Her absence, then actual received farewell letter, precede the marriage news (P95–154). Do not insert an unshown sexual liaison or treat her expressed unavoidable noble obligations as a freely preferred exit.

An unnamed household gatekeeper refuses the party entry without giving reasons (P163–167); identity and whose specific order are unprovided. The18-year-old male warrior candidate advertises sword/shield role and actually withdraws after Megumin’s introduction (P209–246); no match to another warrior by age/class. Joseph/ジョセフ is named in a shouted report of a farm injury (P276), not a directly verified permanent disability or death. Dust’s actual defensive effort has costs and does not perform like Darkness’s exceptional durability (P284–300). These are source-bound follow-up leads, not automatically new census people.

The unnamed young noble speaks of affection across class and asks Leen about photographs (P394–410); K/Dust initially infer the wrong target. Leen later says his desired subject was Dust (P502–507). Dust and K intrude, misuse property and are discovered; the noble then interprets Dust’s defiant statements as reciprocal acceptance (P487–489). A scream is heard after the door closes (P509–511), but the source does not show a completed sexual assault or establish consent to one. Leen’s laughter/fatalistic joke is not Dust’s permission. No name or explicit join to Aigis/Undain/a helmeted noble is given here. Leen’s final Alderp-marriage news is a report of town rumor (P516–523), not a witnessed earlier contract or completed marriage.

K explicitly identifies the marriage news as Leen's secondhand report and withholds a firm account until meeting Darkness (P27–30). Norris/ノリス is a named household night watchman whose small-sound concern was accurate despite his colleague's smallheartedness judgment (P108–117). K impersonates his voice after Aqua's actual entertainer support (P125–150); later statements by that voice are K's inventions, not Norris's conduct. The unnamed cook agrees to a counterfeit order without seeing the speaker (P142–160), not evidence of Alderp's control. Norris requires an existing-census and literal retrieval check before new-row treatment.

Darkness herself says she ordered the party not admitted (P175), resolving the prior gatekeeper's refusal without assigning Alderp an unshown order. K physically restrains her and repeatedly counterfeits her speech; sexual claims to the household are his fabrications, and the rescue-purpose claim does not erase coercion. Darkness's actual debt account says Alderp used her father's worsening condition to demand repayment or marriage cancellation of debt (P298–306); her jokes about sex coexist the narrator's perception of loneliness (P307–308), not freely preferred marriage. Debt origin and illness cause are not yet established. She refuses commoners' lifesaving earnings as repayment and says K's present wealth insufficient (P310), not an exact debt amount.

Darkness's proposed intimacy does not produce intercourse; the exchange collapses after K's abdominal remark (P329–358). Ignis is visibly emaciated/weak, yet attentive and capable of humor and resource planning (P434–463). K's claim he instantly infers the visit's purpose is narrator interpretation. Ignis requests escape for his daughter, withholds debt origin except her decision, proposes sale of the house and says other efforts might remove debt (P454–466): possibilities, not completed legal relief. His daughter-character praise and belief she likes K are his own partial fatherly account, not omniscient relationship facts. He says poison was checked and not found (P475–480), not a source-level proof of no supernatural harm. His expected rejection of royal tax-funded relief is his prediction of Darkness's principle (P488–491), not an observed royal refusal or proof he lacks all influence. He is physically limited, not morally/passively absent; actual marriage is still prospective. Darkness explicitly cites harm transferred to others if she flees (P503), a stated reason rather than evidence of every specific consequence.

Alderp's publicity spending and expedited schedule are K's received account with inferential motive (P6–11). The Dustiness head butler explicitly names himself Hagen/ハーゲン (P62), politely brings the daily threatening letters and warns against escalation (P66–72); the letter actually read is a threat framed as a protective warning (P73), not proof of a real Demon Army terrorist. Megumin's subsequent detention and release through the household are retrospective report (P102–104). Hagen later actually arranges Aqua's noon service while avoiding the escalating devil/goddess confrontation (P248–261); he is NOT the rude unnamed Alderp messenger. K's investigations report alleged sexual coercion, extortion/bribery and absent material proof, plus Ignis's assigned oversight role (P155–164): attributed research, not every allegation performed in view. Vanir's debt-origin account identifies the surviving agricultural/infrastructure losses, Alderp's alleged compensation refusal and redirection of responsibility, Dustiness's spent assets, new loan and bodily collateral condition (P269–300). This is Vanir's account rather than a newly watched historical negotiation. K joins the old butler visit and Hydra effort by inference (P304–308). Vanir withholds explanation until an actual commercial transaction and states his shared interest and price advantage (P212–235/313); do not turn the assistance into disinterested benevolence or full independent validation of every allegation.

Focalization explicitly changes to Darkness, then returns to K from P407. The new maid's congratulation is explained by her ignorance of the circumstances (P319–324), not knowing endorsement of coercion. The long-serving unnamed Dustiness guard actually refuses Alderp access before the ceremony, keeps the legal/household boundary despite a direct threat against his future employment and body of the bride (P327–349), then says he plans to resign rather than serve Alderp. His familiar childhood ball-game role and Darkness's later understanding of it are her recollection/interpretation (P340–347), not performed childhood events. He is not explicitly named Norris, Hagen, an earlier gatekeeper or any other watchman; preserve a source-bound distinct identity pending joins. His sincere admonition about solitary sexual activity rests on K's earlier counterfeit speech (P355–359), a consequential error rather than actual evidence against Darkness. Darkness explicitly calls the marriage unrewarding self-sacrifice, plans to investigate Alderp, and says she now finds him unattractive (P324–325/368–388); earlier masochistic jokes are not blanket consent. Hagen is the longest-serving butler and actually escorts her (P398–403).

Alderp stares at the bride, is briefly checked by Hagen's cough (P426–431), then publicly abuses class and treats the debt as a purchase condition (P469–480). K actually produces 2 billion Eris and Alderp diverts attention to collecting coins while issuing pursuit orders (P475–484/520–528). The command to abandon pursuit and gather money at P522 is K's supported voice imitation, NOT Alderp's real order; actual Alderp immediately contradicts it (P526). His servants show their own tactical limits, react to injury/threat and request he stop provoking Megumin (P575–584), rather than perfectly obeying every demand. Alderp's claim that her city-center Explosion is a bluff is his actual mistaken risk appraisal; the spell later fires into the sky and cracks windows (P630–643), with real collateral cost. His offers of money and secure household employment fail to move watching adventurers (P607–613). Their later intervention includes Dust/Keith's transparently inconsistent injury allegations and an actual beating of the servants (P672–692); their helpful role does not validate the claimed fractures/paralysis or erase harm. K's ownership language and Darkness's arousal are not a general ownership ethic or consent to Alderp. The interrupted ceremonial vows are distinct from the subsequent legal-registration discussion.

Ignis is still severely weak and expects death, but actually welcomes the failed marriage, thanks K, presses a match, asks what his daughter values, and offers a final written intervention (P712–758). His perceived insight into K's feelings remains K's interpretation (P746–748). Aqua actually casts Sacred Break Spell, followed by visible recovery (P761–774), and identifies a major devil's curse (P773). Thus poison-negative testing was not a successful supernatural differential diagnosis; no actual death/resurrection occurs. The father's embarrassed withdrawal under the covers after recovery (P776–777) belongs beside his serious parental affection and institutional initiative. The writing and any legal protection are offered here, not already completed.

Alderp is the first-person focalizer. He actually kicks the crouching devil, identifies his purchased magical coercion, admits exploiting forgotten payment and seeks an overnight universal witness-memory cover-up (P6–32); Maxwell states church/light limits and inability, not a cast visibly failing. Alderp's expectation of executing K and obtaining Darkness's self-sacrifice is prospective (P20–21). His new wish is not performed: Maxwell explicitly says he has done nothing when Vanir's disguised knock arrives (P40–45). Alderp mistakes desire-compatible appearance for success, promises payment and terminates the contract (P44/86–93); subsequent apology/body offer is Vanir impersonating Darkness, not Darkness's consent or a Maxwell transport. Maxwell refuses the now-released order to kill a fellow devil (P63–69). Vanir explicitly joins Maks to Maxwell (P73–80); titles, other-world memory loss, hundreds/thousands of prior introductions, lucky summoning and career dependence are his attributed explanations, not an omniscient total biography. Alderp's lower-devil judgment and self-made-career claim are contradicted by that account but remain his own defensiveness (P80–84). He claims he would have returned Maxwell if asked, a self-serving counterfactual (P98), not proof the elaborate intervention was necessary or unnecessary. Vanir openly credits amusement as his reason and reports accommodating Aqua's egg care (P96–104). Maxwell actually breaks both arms and enjoys the cries (P115–125), then interprets Alderp's desperate appeal as reciprocal affection while promising preserved, prolonged despair (P139–162). His nonpayment victimization does not erase his agency in torture, nor does childish/memory-impaired presentation establish a medical diagnosis. Vanir's contract-years/asset seizure/hell-transport/treatment statements are explanations and predictions (P127–137); full transfer, all future collection and eternal outcome are NOT watched here. Alderp's late apology, attempted asset bargaining, terror and prayer are observable self-preservation, not established remorse or erased harm. Vanir anticipates a household-substitute offer before Alderp completes it (P135–137): do not quote it as a finished spoken order by Alderp.

source_receiving_annotation_history.judgment: Darkness reports Alderp's disappearance, new evidence and probable body-swap gift attribution (Ep1 P9–12); public flight theory is not a witnessed account of his fate. Repayment and asset calculations are prospective pending her father's recovery (P35–41), not payment already received in this scene. Her hypnosis-like retrospective doubt is a report, not proof Maxwell authored every prior choice. Aqua wrongly suspects Vanir of the curse (P33), contrary to the separate interlude causal chain; preserve that information asymmetry. Aqua's stated practice is marriage registration on the morning before vows, leading the party to presume Darkness legally married despite the disrupted ceremony (P129–147); no actual registry document or completed annulment is shown here. Ep2 Chris reports finding and collecting the summoning object in the cellar (P17–22), then actually slips into Eris's voice and supplies its sealed lake hiding place (P49–53). This resolves the earlier search's false-negative location account without pretending the search was exhaustive. K still lacks the interlude knowledge of the devil arrangement. No exact later fate for Alderp or royal/body-swap victims beyond the reported/prospective statements is imported.

source_receiving_annotation_history.scope: MAIN05 Ep/start p-020 complete P1–96; household-name retrieval and census check
source_receiving_annotation_history.judgment: Darkness explicitly recognizes the assaulted caller as Hagen/ハーゲン, her household servant (P44–52), an earlier join to the same named role, not Rionor's or MAIN11 Heidel's butler. Hagen endures K/Aqua's unprovoked attack, regains breath and delivers a royal letter (P38–52/69–72). He also makes belittling/sexualized statements about Darkness having only noble status and selling her body if that status is lost (P60–68), then fears her actual choking. His formal service is not uniform tact or spotless guardianship; his institutional fear does not excuse the insults. The 41-native-object literal search for ハーゲン/ノリス/ジョセフ checked every current register and found five resources, zero XML failures and zero semantic credit. Existing census row114 is Hagen, so retain/enrich that record; Norris/Joseph lack an exact named row in this targeted check. Role overlap for the unnamed wedding guard remains unproved. The earlier broad census read output was truncated and confers no complete-row review credit; the later bounded selected fields were actually received.

K's retrospective narration reports actual confiscation and transfer of Alderp's assets to Ignis, Balter's non-involvement/no punishment and future role assisting the new lord (P14–20); it is not a directly watched investigation or Balter's own acceptance speech. Ignis remains not fully recovered and Darkness temporarily governs, preserving capacity constraints rather than instant complete restoration. K later says the money has been returned (P113), a later reported outcome distinct from the earlier prospective refund. Vanir admits other solutions existed and that he selected the elaborate wedding humiliation for its emotional flavor (P120/134); do not claim necessity. Aqua/Wiz/Darkness still conflate Vanir with the dangerous cursing devil, while Vanir attributes it to another major devil (P129–139). Their group conclusion is a mistake, not source validation that Vanir cast the curse. No fresh Alderp or Maxwell choice appears here.

source_receiving_annotation_history.scope: MAIN09 C2/start part0011 P440–570; MAIN12 C5/start part0014 P270–390; MAIN13 C2/start part0011 P300–410; MAIN14 C3/start part0012 P1–165
source_receiving_annotation_history.judgment: MAIN09 P507 names Alderp only in K's recollection of the marriage crisis and an earlier failed/ discarded explosive imitation; no current lord action. MAIN12 P328 uses Alderp as a fearful analogy before meeting Zereschilt, not proof every noble or the new host behaves like him. The guards' actual negotiation and host's different identity remain separate actors. MAIN13 P356 is K's recollection that losing Darkness exposed the party's dependence, not a new Alderp interaction or revised principal score. MAIN14 P110 is Darkness's own grievance about K's wedding rescue and ownership declaration amid current relationship conflict; it is not Alderp speaking, a new attempted marriage or generic consent to ownership. These are bounded reference checks rather than complete chapter/whole-volume passes. Other characters present retain their already scoped analyses or future reviews, without silently expanding this cohort's claims.

The accepted principal contract names this member C2/start; do not inherit a mistaken C1 alias. Vanir proposes introducing Maxwell as affectionate/good-looking and from another world (P356), then says the back of the head is physically absent (P359). These are Vanir's matchmaking/joke claims, not a new Maxwell appearance, observed skull examination, psychiatric diagnosis, evidence of a performed date or proof affection is safe. Wiz explicitly says devils have no sex/gender in this exchange (P360); first-person 僕 alone does not establish human maleness. The prior interlude's actual violence qualifies the positive introduction. Amaryllis's con and prior history remain separate characters/access planes. No additional Maxwell reaction or independent trial arises from the reference.

Restaurant patrons credit the unnamed chancellor with prosperity (P235–246); this is overheard public attribution, not a national audit or unmediated performance history. Ragcraft explicitly names himself chancellor when he arrives and quiets the reception (P581–592). He gives a courteous but locally belittling compliment about Iris's clan (P589), shows discomfort under Aqua's touch and questions, and accepts the Axis explanation (P594–602); Aqua's unease is not yet an explicit species diagnosis. At the actual small reception he invokes the intentionally modest hospitality as evidence of financial distress and refuses defense support (P610–631); the prosperous-city contrast is raised by K and Iris. He wrongly treats K's sibling address as evidence of royal/Jatice identity (P624–629), rather than perceiving all disguises.
